(New Orleans, Louisiana) | college = * [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Miss]] (2020–2022) * [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] (2022–2023) * [[Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball|Jacksonville State]] (2024–2025) * [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] (2025–2026) | draftyear=2026 | draftround=2 | draftpick=58 | draftteam=[[New Orleans Pelicans]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years2 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team2 = →[[Laketown Squadron]] | highlights = * [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Conference USA Player of the Year]] (2025) * First-team All-[[Conference USA]] (2025) }} '''Jaron Pierre Jr.''' (born July 12, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Laketown Squadron]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Miss Golden Eagles]], [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]], [[Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball|Jacksonville State Gamecocks]], and [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU Mustangs]]. == High school career == Pierre attended [[St. Augustine High School (New Orleans)|St. Augustine High School]] in [[New Orleans|New Orleans, Louisiana]]. After his high school career, he committed to play college basketball at [[University of Southern Mississippi]].{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=C. C. S. |date=2020-04-16 |title=Recruiting: St. Augustine guard Jaron Pierre signs with Southern Miss basketball |url=https://crescentcitysports.com/recruiting-st-augustine-guard-jaron-pierre-signs-with-southern-miss-basketball/ |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=Crescent City Sports |language=en-US}} == College career == Pierre played two seasons with the Golden Eagles, averaging 8.8 points as a true freshman and 9.9 points as a sophomore.{{Cite web |last=Eldridge |first=Taylor |title=How Jaron Pierre Jr. plans to become a 'smarter' scorer for Wichita State basketball |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article266410346.html |website=Wichita Eagle}} At the conclusion of his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Wichita State University]].{{Cite web |last=Eldridge |first=Taylor |title=Wichita State basketball dips back into transfer portal for team’s sixth 2022 recruit |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article260958702.html |website=Wichita Eagle}} As a junior, he averaged 10.6 points per game before entering the transfer portal for a second time.{{Cite web |last=Eldridge |first=Taylor |title=With Jaron Pierre in transfer portal, Wichita State must replace entire starting lineup |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article274270925.html |website=Wichita Eagle}} Pierre transferred again to [[Grambling State University]] where he reportedly redshirted for the [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Tigers men's basketball]] team for the entire year.{{cite news |last1=Geoghegan |first1=Zack |title=Transfer Portal Bio Blast: Jaron Pierre Jr. |url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/transfer-portal-bio-blast-jaron-pierre-jr/ |access-date=2 July 2026 |work=KSR |date=3 April 2025 |language=en}} However, Pierre was not listed on [[2023–24 Grambling State Tigers men's basketball team|Grambling's 2023–2024 basketball]] roster{{cite web |title=2023-24 Men's Basketball Roster |url=https://gsutigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/2023-24 |publisher=[[Grambling State Tigers|Grambling State University Athletics]] |access-date=2 July 2026 |language=en}} and, according to an interview in [[Southern Methodist University]]'s (SMU's) ''[[The Daily Campus (SMU)|The Daily Campus]]'', he enrolled in Grambling so as to focus on academics, spend a year "without basketball" and [[Self-discovery|find himself]].{{cite news |last1=Welch |first1=Tyler |title=Journeyman Jaron |url=https://smudailycampus.com/1068366/sports/journeyman-jaron/ |access-date=2 July 2026 |work=[[The Daily Campus (SMU)|The Daily Campus]] |date=February 17, 2026}} He transferred for a third time to [[Jacksonville State University]], where he made an instant impact at the beginning of the [[2024–25 Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball team|2024–25 season]].{{Cite web |last=Ashworth |first=Thomas |date=2024-11-19 |title=Jax State guard Jaron Pierre Jr. earns conference, national weekly honors |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2024/11/jax-state-guard-jaron-pierre-jr-earns-conference-national-weekly-honors.html |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=al |language=en}} Against Middle Tennessee State, he scored a career-high 36 points, setting the school record for most points scored in a game at home.{{Cite web |last=Medley |first=Joe |date=2025-02-07 |title=Jacksonville State University's 'Special Player' |url=https://calhounjournal.com/jacksonville-state-universitys-special-player/ |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=Calhoun Journal |language=en-US}} At the conclusion of the season, Pierre was named [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Conference USA Player of the Year]]{{Cite web |last=Ashworth |first=Thomas |date=2025-03-10 |title=Jax State's Harper named CUSA Coach of Year, Pierre named player of the year |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2025/03/jax-states-harper-named-cusa-coach-of-year-pierre-named-player-of-the-year.html |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=al |language=en}}{{Cite web |author=Staff Reports |date=2025-03-10 |title=Jax State's Pierre, Harper garner major CUSA men's basketball honors |url=https://www.annistonstar.com/sports/jsu/jax-states-pierre-harper-garner-major-cusa-mens-basketball-honors/article_c9723132-fde4-11ef-be19-63fa8c0ec9c2.html |access-date=2025-03-10 |website=The Anniston Star |language=en}} and subsequently put his name in the [[transfer portal]] while putting his name in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web |first=Richie |last=Mills |title=Jaron Pierre enters transfer portal while testing NBA Draft waters |url=https://wgno.com/sports/jaron-pierre-enters-transfer-portal-while-testing-nba-draft-waters/ |website=[[WGNO]] |date=March 31, 2025 |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} Following the season he had at Jacksonville, Pierre transferred to [[Southern Methodist University|SMU]] and subsequently withdrew his name from the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=“Highlights so crazy you have to watch it twice”: Fans approve as Jaron Pierre Jr withdraws from NBA draft for SMU |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/college-basketball/highlights-crazy-watch-twice-fans-approve-jaron-pierre-jr-withdraws-nba-draft-smu |website=[[Sportskeeda]] |date=May 28, 2026 |access-date=July 16, 2026 |first=Geoffrey |last=Latayan }}{{cite web |title=Jaron Pierre commits to SMU |url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2025/4/14/24408631/jaron-pierre-commits-smu-mustangs-basketball-kentucky-transfers-nba-draft-2025 |website=A Sea of Blue |first=Jason |last=Marcum |date=April 14, 2025 |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} During his singular season at SMU, he appeared in every single game for the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball| Mustangs]]. At the conclusion of the season, Pierre averaged 17.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.1 assists. On March 18, 2026, shortly after the regular season, SMU played against the [[2025–26 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami RedHawks]] in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2026 March Madness tournament]], where in his lone March Madness appearance, Pierre scored 18 points, four rebounds, assists, and three steals in 39 minutes of playtime in a ten-point 79-89 loss to the team.{{cite web |title=Jaron Pierre Jr. |url=https://www.rotowire.com/cbasketball/player/jaron-pierre-17042 |website=[[RotoWire]] |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} On April 15, 2026, Pierre announced on [[Instagram]] that he had declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=The work was hidden. The blessing won’t be. — Matthew 6:18” |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DXLETVgDKqD/ |website=[[Instagram]] |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} On July 15, 2026, Pierre was named for the NABC Team Academic Excellence Honoree award.{{cite web |title=SMU Named NABC Team Academic Excellence Honoree, Three Mustangs Earn Spot On The Honors Court |url=https://smumustangs.com/news/2026/7/15/mens-basketball-smu-named-nabc-team-academic-excellence-honoree-three-mustangs-earn-spot-on-the-honors-court.aspx |website=[[SMU Mustangs]] |publisher=[[Southern Methodist University Athletics]] |date=July 15, 2026 |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} ==Professional career== On June 24, 2026, Pierre was selected with the 58th overall pick by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |title=Pick 58: Jaron Pierre Jr. joins the Pelicans during the 2026 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/videos/jaron-pierre-jr-2026-nba-draft-pick-58 |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} Pierre became the first SMU draft pick following the draft of [[Shake Milton]] in 2018,{{cite web |title=Jaron Pierre Jr. taken by Pelicans at No. 58, marking first SMU draft pick since 2018 |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/smu-mustangs/article/jaron-pierre-jr-pelicans-nba-draft-smu-mustangs-22319871.php |website=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} he also became the first [[New Orleans]] native to be drafted by the team.{{cite web |title=Jaron Pierre Jr. becomes first New Orleans native drafted by Pelicans|url=https://www.fox8live.com/2026/06/25/jaron-pierre-jr-becomes-first-new-orleans-native-drafted-by-pelicans/ |website=[[WVUE-DT|Fox 8]] |date=June 25, 2026 |access-date=July 16, 2026 }} On July 24, Pierre signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pelicans and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Laketown Squadron]].{{cite web|title= New Orleans Pelicans sign Jaron Pierre Jr. to two-way contract|url= https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-jaron-pierre-jr-two-way-contract-7-23-2026|date=July 24,
